sections.h2: Selling routes for a Union City homeowner
sections.html:
Owners here usually choose among an agent listing, a for-sale-by-owner approach, and a direct purchase by a cash buyer. The cash route wins on speed when the house needs work, carries a tax balance or has tenants in it.

Union City lies in southern Fulton County, so most paperwork passes through Fulton offices plus the city's Community Development and Finance departments. Sorting those out first shortens nearly any sale. Before you talk to buyers:

  • Pull your deed and the current mortgage payoff statement.
  • Look for open building permits or code citations tied to the address.
  • Make sure city and county taxes are paid up.
  • Gather HOA documents if your street has covenants.

Cash offers generally come in below a repaired and staged listing, and the exchange is certainty and speed. Weigh what you would net after repairs, carrying costs and an agent's commission against the quick close.

Union City is a small community in the southern part of Fulton County, roughly fifteen minutes from Atlanta and ten miles from Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport. Buyers who commute or fly often value that airport distance. Atlanta Metro Studios, one of the region's large production facilities, is also in the city.

Population has climbed from 19,456 in 2010 to 26,830 in 2020, with an estimate of 29,910 for July 1, 2025. Land area barely changed, 19.11 square miles in 2010 and 19.67 in 2020, so the new households arrived inside a nearly fixed footprint. Demand for housing here is real.

Owners occupy 40.4 percent of Union City homes, which makes rental houses a big slice of the market. Numbers are 2020 to 2024 estimates unless dated.

Landlords selling a rented house are a familiar sight in these numbers. Read the lease before you list, since the tenant's term and any notice terms travel with the sale.

The city's own taxes ride on the Fulton County bill. The city's 2026 millage rate is 11.296, split into 11.132 for maintenance and operations and 0.164 for bonds.

Existing homestead, disability, disabled veteran and senior exemptions on city taxes stay in place without a new application, and new Senior Homestead applications go to Fulton County directly. The city itself still collects unpaid 2024 and earlier balances, which can carry interest, penalties and tax sale proceedings.

Fulton splits the work in two. The Board of Assessors keeps ownership and mailing records, sets values and takes homestead applications and appeals. The Tax Commissioner builds the bill and collects payment.

  • Fulton County Tax Commissioner: 404-613-6100
  • Fulton County Board of Assessors: 404-612-6440

Clear any older city balance on your parcel before closing, since the title search will surface it.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Fulton assessment
sections.html:
Owners get 45 days from the date on the Notice of Assessment. Notices are posted online in June, and the notice itself shows your exact deadline, so read it the day it arrives.

Only the assessed value can be appealed, and the estimated tax cannot. File online at the county assessor site, in person or by mail, then pick a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration on value, or a Hearing Officer, where fees may apply for the last two. Appeals can take months, and a temporary tax bill may arrive during the wait. Pay it, or penalties follow.

The South Fulton Service Center of the Board of Assessors sits at 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, Suite 224, and the phone is 404-612-6440. The standard homestead deadline is April 1, with a second window during the appeal period for owners who qualified as of January 1.

Most construction needs a building permit from the city, and work starts only once it is issued. A permit lapses when construction fails to begin within 180 days or stops for 180 consecutive days.

Permit applications, plan submittals, invoice payment and inspection scheduling run through the city's IWORQ online portal. Inspection requests need the permit number and contractor code, and requests for next-business-day inspection must come in before 4:00 pm Eastern. The Community Development office is at 5041 Union St, open Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and permit questions go to 770-515-7950, option 1.

Code Enforcement accepts violations by phone, fax, email or area survey, and an officer investigates within 24 hours of a report. Its phone line is (770) 515-7890, Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Officers inspecting one property may also survey adjacent properties, so a neighbor's complaint can lead to a look at your yard.

The Planning Division posts the current zoning ordinance, development regulations and subdivision regulations, along with the Comprehensive Plan and Future Land Use Map. Look up the zoning on your parcel if a buyer plans a particular use.

The deed goes to the Fulton County Clerk of Superior Court once Georgia's transfer tax is paid. The seller is liable unless the contract shifts it to the buyer. The state's printed rate sits on its Department of Revenue page.

Fulton County Schools serves Union City. Its South Learning Center is at 4025 Flat Shoals Road in Union City, and the district publishes an address lookup showing the elementary, middle and high school zones for any home. Share that result when a buyer asks.

If taxes or a code citation turn up during the title search, they get paid or cleared from your proceeds at closing. Raising them yourself before you list avoids a surprise at the table.

A rough order of events for a quick sale: collect your documents, confirm the tax and permit status with the offices above, accept an offer, open title, pay off the lender and any city balance, then sign and record the deed. A cash buyer shortens the middle of that list because there is no loan approval to wait for.

Tenants change the picture. If someone is renting the house, tell every bidder up front, hand over the lease, and agree on whether it will be sold occupied or delivered empty.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Union City?
faqs.a: Fulton County sends one bill that carries the city portion. The city's 2026 millage is 11.296, and delinquent balances from 2024 and earlier stay with the city.

faqs.q: Is a city inspection required before I sell in Union City?
faqs.a: No sale inspection is part of the permit process. The city does require permits for most construction and runs inspections through the online portal, so confirm that past work was permitted and signed off.

faqs.q: What if I miss the Fulton assessment appeal deadline?
faqs.a: You lose the right to appeal that year's value once the printed date passes. Watch the date on each year's notice, which gives 45 days, and file early online or at a Board of Assessors office.

faqs.q: Can I report a code problem next door before I list?
faqs.a: Yes. Reports go in by phone at (770) 515-7890, fax, email or through an area survey during an inspection, and an officer looks into it within 24 hours. Clearing an eyesore early helps showings.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Union City homes?
faqs.a: Fulton County Schools. Its South Learning Center is on Flat Shoals Road in Union City, and the district's address lookup shows the elementary, middle and high school zones for your house.
